## Context / Problem
The op-cert service currently owns per-job boto3/SSM/region lookup and patches process-global key/principal/push state. That couples application configuration to one deployment secret store, permits jobs to observe different keys inside one process, and creates concurrency/cleanup hazards. ADR 0098 retains SSM as a deployment storage option but moves application binding to startup.

## Outcome
At service startup accept exactly one of preferred `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` or compatibility `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY`. Validate before queue/worker/network/workspace creation, copy into a process-owned 0700 directory/0600 file, build one immutable signer/runtime, and pass signer/principal/push policy context-locally to jobs. The running process never rereads/reloads; restart observes replacement. Remove application runtime SSM/boto3/region coupling and per-job retrieval.

## Plan
1. Replace `opcert_service.ssm`/per-job key acquisition with startup composition in config/key-provider/app. Reject missing, both-set, unreadable, non-regular, wrong-mode where required, malformed, encrypted/passphrase, or non-Ed25519 input before service work.
2. Copy key bytes to a new process-owned runtime directory/file at 0700/0600; never modify/delete the deployment source. Cleanup removes only Rebar's copy on graceful shutdown. Deployment tmpfs/restart owns crash cleanup.
3. Replace global environment/state patching with typed context-local signer, environment principal, and push policy passed through jobs/workspace/signing. Concurrent and timed-out workers cannot observe or mutate one another's context.
4. Update compose/Dockerfile/deployment bootstrap so SSM-at-rest may be materialized/mounted before process startup, but the application container receives the file/value contract and no SSM parameter/region permission for key retrieval.
5. Preserve ADR 0049's Ed25519/DSSE algorithm, trust roots/eras, producer, authoritative fetch, envelope persistence, guard, and no-workspace-push invariants.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- Startup component tests instrument queue, worker, network, and workspace factories and assert every invalid source fails before all four.
- Filesystem tests assert source untouched, process directory 0700, copy 0600, stable bytes after source replacement, restart observes new bytes, graceful cleanup removes only copy, and stale tmpfs clears in container restart canary.
- Concurrent/timed-out job tests use distinct principals/policies and prove context isolation, immutable startup signer, existing producer signatures, and no workspace push remote.
- Structural tests assert `src/rebar/opcert_service` has no boto3/SSM/region import or runtime parameter after cutover; deployment assertions retain optional SSM-at-rest materialization outside the application.
- [operator-attested] Hosted op-cert/review-bot signing canary records deployment/run ids, source kind (never value/path), signature verification, restart result, modes, timestamp, and redacted failure outcome.

## Compatibility / rollback
Expand deployment input first while the legacy per-job facade exists. Before removal, rollback selects the legacy facade. After removal, rollback requires the same startup source contract; signatures/envelopes remain compatible. Inline multiline environment input remains a documented weaker compatibility source and is removed from unrelated children.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Exactly-one source validation rejects every named invalid case before queue, worker, network, or workspace construction.
- [ ] The process-owned copy is 0700/0600, stable for process lifetime, observes replacement only after restart, and cleanup never alters the deployment source.
- [ ] Concurrent and timed-out jobs prove context-local signer/principal/push isolation, one immutable startup signer, existing signature verification, and no workspace push remote.
- [ ] Application runtime has no SSM/boto3/region/key-parameter dependency; deployment may still materialize ADR 0049's SSM value before startup.
- [ ] Secret/key sentinels are absent from repr, serialization, argv, logs, exceptions, output, fingerprints, provenance, children, and persisted envelopes beyond the existing public signature.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Hosted signing/restart/tmpfs canaries pass with the required redacted evidence recorded.
